# ADR-021: Use one operation-owned collision cursor for typed source dispatch

Status: chosen_for_partial_collision_dispatch

Concerns: Q-state, Q-behavior, Q-evidence

## Decision

Generate a typed CollisionPass that captures vector size and source owner identity once. next_source_collision rereads current IDs/LastC for every notice. dispatch_source_collisions drives that same cursor and emits immediate typed host-error notices while continuing after a false host result.

## Rationale

A copied event batch would lose force/ID mutations and nested calls. The unchanged C++ dispatcher shows appended contacts are outside the current captured count, while recursive dispatch captures its own count and observes current data.

## Alternatives

Prebuilding a whole event payload list, deduplicating IDs, sharing a global cursor, serializing f64 through JSON on the typed core path, or substituting an end-of-tick event drain for per-body publication.

## Consequences

Six independent C++ cases yield 319 contacts and three host-error notices, including same-owner recursive dispatch. Typed real-gradient output, nesting, foreign-world/owner replacement and unsafe-list-shrink handling have headless witnesses. Automatic missile publication/FFI wiring and mandatory proof/host/lifetime correspondence remain open.
